newsitem.title: USA: Hudson Foods disputes OSHA allegations.
newsitem.headline: Hudson Foods disputes OSHA allegations.

text.p: Hudson Foods Inc on Tuesday disputed contentions by the U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration that it allegedly violated worker safety requirements at its Noel, Mo., plant.

Hudson's Senior Director of Corporate Marketing John White said in a statement that the company is "absolute stunned" by the agency's remarks that the company "endangered workers by blocking fire and emergency exits" and failed to give cleanup crews proper protection against chemicals that resulted in serious eye injuries.

"Those statements do not reflect the reality of Hudson Foods' 25-year record in plant safety, nor our relationship with our associates," White said. "Hudson Foods prides itself on being a company with a strong safety and health program and our record reflects that."
OSHA has issued a citation and proposed $332,500 in penalties against Hudson Foods for the alleged violations.
The company said that the OSHA notification it received Tuesday said, "this citation does not constitute a finding that a violation has occurred."
